problem: Suppose that $f(x)$ is a  function such that ${\int }_{2}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x=8$ and ${\int }_{2}^{0}2f(x)\,\text{d}x=4.$ What is the value of ${\int }_{0}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x?$

feedback.worked_solution:
Let's simplify one of the given integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{8}^{3}\frac{5}{2}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x & =15 \\ \frac{5}{2}{\int }_{8}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =15 \\ -\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{3}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =15 \\ {\int }_{3}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-6\end{aligned}
$$

Then, from the adjacent intervals rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{7}{2}+(-6) \\  & =-\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
